repairs.text: Strongest feature: Aron Ra converts Hernandez’s claim that a soul animates the body into an empirical inference: if a distinct entity controls, leaves, or enters bodies, its causal activity should produce observable consequences even when the entity itself remains undetected. Principal limitation: The vehicle and passenger analogy may overstate Hernandez’s embodied account as an independently operating occupant, while offering no discriminating experiment, measurement, or predicted result that separates rival explanations. Live burden: Aron Ra must derive consequences from Hernandez’s actual view and explain why their presence or absence is likelier if brains produce mental life than if souls act only through brains. Locked score: The locked score of 81 fits because the testability challenge is coherent, responsive, and burden-focused, yet its comparative predictions and charitable specification remain compressed.

Strongest feature: Aron Ra targets “animates” in Hernandez’s definition by invoking modern biology’s ability to explain metabolism, reproduction, regulation, and organismal activity without an additional life force, thereby removing a traditional explanatory task assigned to souls. Principal limitation: The compressed claim that vitalism was disproved does not distinguish that discarded biological force from Hernandez’s proposed consciousness-bearing substantial subject, so defeating the former neither directly tests nor refutes the latter. Live burden: Aron Ra must either confine his conclusion to biological animation or establish that Hernandez’s soul duplicates vitalism’s obsolete causal role instead of describing consciousness’s relation to a body already alive. Locked score: The locked score of 71 fits because biological sufficiency narrows the soul’s work, while conflation and restricted reach leave the central consciousness claim substantially untouched.
